text:
maya: quick async standup — SLOs / alerts / oncall follow-ups

maya: what I did yesterday: rolled out batcher backpressure fix to two canaries, patched autoscaler policy to avoid rapid scale-down on short bursts, landed PR #4821 (batcher:reduce-queue-fallthrough).

maya: blockers: still seeing intermittent 504s at ~p50-p95 during peak traffic; logs point to KV cache eviction spikes when instances restart. can't repro locally.

alex: saw similar spikes in eu-west yesterday. i dug into the eviction metrics — there are bursts right after deploys. could be race in warmup.

javier: can you paste the prom query for the eviction spike? i can run a short lookback.

maya: sure — this is what I used:
```
sum by(instance) (increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m]))
```
looks like a cluster of instances had >100 evictions in a 5m window.

lisa: fwiw, we had a related pager at 03:12 UTC Friday with the same signature. postmortem link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-739 (notes in the incident comment).

alex: suggestion: add a brief warmup at instance startup that hits `GET /health?warmup=true` which primes the KV with common prefixes. also throttle the eviction worker for first 2 minutes. low-risk change.

maya: i'll open two PRs: one for the warmup (light touch) and one to add a circuit-breaker around eviction concurrency. will link them here.

oncall-bot: alert: inference-504-rate increased (threshold breached) — rule: inference.504.rate > 0.5% over 5m — triggered at 1767775112. Pager: maya, alex.

maya: acked oncall-bot. i'll take initial triage and mute noisy duplicates.

javier: quick question — do we want to adjust alert threshold temporarily while we push the warmup? we should avoid noisy pages but not mask real regressions.

lisa: i'd favor a short-term suppression on duplicate alerts for the same instance for 30m + a runbook note. then fast rollback if errors rise.

alex: agreed. i'll craft a runbook blurb and a PROM tweak and post as a PR against infra-alerts.

maya: PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/197 (warmup), https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/198 (eviction-circuit). requesting @lisa and @alex for review.

maya: today plan: 1) finish instrumentation on eviction path and add additional logging, 2) push warmup PR, 3) monitor SLO dashboard and mute noisy dupes, 4) follow up with oncall handover notes.

alex: i'll review the PRs this morning and prepare alert suppression patch.

javier: i'll run a 24h lookback query and post a small heatmap in the #eng-sre dashboard thread.

lisa: pinged security for a quick eyes-on the warmup endpoint (should be read-only).

maya: thanks — will update here after PRs merge. :thumbsup:
